title: steward/v2
description: targets/<id>/stewards/<n>.yaml (F23-R8, R9; D-32 v3.33, D-22 v3.33): one signed act by a steward, as steward/v1, made either with the steward's own SSH key or through the service with the network's approval key (`via`). v2 adds `via` and `admitted_by`, and makes `link` optional while admission is open. A record whose signature does not verify, whose `via: approval-key` key differs from keys/approval.pub in the merge's parent tree, or whose `admitted_by` disagrees with policy.json's steward_admission is refused at the gate by name. A step-down of either version may end a commitment of either version for the same login. Versioned, never edited (D-34).

login.description: The steward's GitHub login (the login grammar: alphanumerics and single hyphens, at most 39 characters). Validated before it enters any message or page (F15 §7).

name.description: The steward's display name, as they wish to be named on the target page (D-32 v3.17). Free text, escaped wherever it is shown.

link.description: One identity link (an institutional page or an ORCID record), which a curator reads before merging under `reviewed` admission (D-22 v3.33). Optional under `open`. Rendered as a link only after the record validates, through the site's allowlist (F11-Q11).

commitment.description: The fixed sentence for the action, verbatim (opn_gate.steward.COMMITMENT for a commit, STEP_DOWN for a step-down). A record with any other text counts for nothing.

via.description: How the signature was made (D-3, D-32 v3.33): `ssh`, by the signer's own SSH key; `approval-key`, by the network's approval key through the service, for a login signed in with GitHub on the site, in which case `key` must equal the graph's keys/approval.pub in the merge's parent tree.

admitted_by.description: Who admitted the steward (D-32 v3.33): `self` under policy.json's `open` admission; under `reviewed`, the login of the curator who merges the record.

key.description: The SSH public key the signature verifies under: the steward's own (`via: ssh`) or the network's approval key (`via: approval-key`).

signature.description: An OpenSSH SSHSIG armored signature over the record's canonical body, made with the private half of `key`.
